title: Emrys and the Monsoon
premise: Felix Fairweather, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Vane Syndicate—a crew of cheerful, ruthless lenders—takes one last paid job: flying weather support for a scientific expedition up the Kessari River during monsoon season. When the expedition's radio goes silent, Felix is the only pilot crazy enough to fly in, and what she finds upriver is a discovery worth killing for: a living storm system that seems to respond to human presence. The Syndicate wants it weaponized; the expedition wants it protected; Felix must choose between paying her debts with the truth or going home empty-handed and hunted. In the end she burns the evidence, turns herself over to the storm rather than the Syndicate, and walks out of the flood zone alive but unproven—free, finally, because no one believes what she saw.
about_author: Lena Marchetti is a former river guide who spent six seasons on monsoon-fed waterways before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure stories about people whose survival depends on knowing when to run and when to stand still.

chapters.title: Debt of Clear Skies
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She lands her battered plane in Port Calloway hours ahead of a debt collector, establishing her pattern: keep moving, never land twice. A Syndicate 'optimist' named Bright finds her anyway and offers a way out—one season of weather support for an upriver expedition. Beat: desperation dressed as opportunity.

chapters.title: The Manifest
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She reviews the expedition roster—six scientists, a doctor, a botanist named Ilsa Voss who seems to know more about the river than the maps do—and signs a contract whose fine print she deliberately doesn't read. Emotional beat: willful blindness as survival strategy.

chapters.title: Monsoon Rules
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, opening leg of the journey. She teaches the team how to read monsoon weather while privately noting that Ilsa reads clouds better than she does. First radio check-ins go smoothly; the river feels generous. Beat: false camaraderie, the calm before the season turns.

chapters.title: Static on the Third Week
chapters.summary: Felix's POV from base camp at the river mouth. The expedition's scheduled check-in doesn't come, then misses the backup window. The Syndicate's handler tells her to wait it out; her gut says fly. Beat: the moment staying invisible stops being possible.

chapters.title: Flying Into the Wall
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Against orders she flies upriver through a squall line that shouldn't be there—it's rotating wrong, building wrong. She crash-lands short of the last known camp and continues on foot. Beat: commitment past the point of return.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She finds the abandoned camp: equipment intact, food untouched, but every radio dismantled with surgical care. No bodies. One boot print, barefoot, leading into flooded forest. Beat: dread shifting from disaster to something deliberate.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Voice
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV, flashback three weeks earlier. The team found the anomaly—a standing supercell that hasn't moved in months—and Ilsa realized it responds to sound, to voices, almost like attention. She ordered the radios destroyed before anyone could report it. Beat: the discovery and the first moral fracture.

chapters.title: The Standing Storm
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She reaches the anomaly itself: a tower of cloud fixed over a drowned valley, lightning crawling its flanks in patterns too regular. When she shouts into the wind, the wind answers back in kind. Beat: awe curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Survivors
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She finds four of the seven expedition members living in a cave beneath the storm's rain shadow, healthy and strangely reluctant to leave. Their leader, Dr. Anselm, speaks of the storm like a colleague. Beat: rescue complicated by the rescued not wanting rescue.

chapters.title: Bright Ideas
chapters.summary: Bright's POV. At base camp, the Syndicate decodes fragments of the expedition's early transmissions and realizes what's upriver. Bright is dispatched with salvage crews and a smile. Beat: the true stakes arrive—the storm is now an asset with a price tag.

chapters.title: Three Missing
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. He confesses to Felix that he sent three members downriver to get help against Ilsa's wishes; they never arrived. Ilsa took two others deeper toward the storm's eye. The team is splitting along the fault line of what the discovery owes the world. Beat: loyalty vs. truth made flesh.

chapters.title: The Eye Is a Room
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Following Ilsa's trail, Felix enters the storm's calm center and finds a hollow of still air where sound behaves like memory—the storm replays voices spoken inside it. She hears her own name, spoken by someone who died years ago. Beat: the personal cost of the discovery.

chapters.title: Terms of Survival
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa explains her plan: seal the valley, let the storm stay unknown, because anything measured gets owned. She offers Felix erasure—her debts, her record, her old life—in exchange for silence. Beat: temptation with a clean conscience attached.

chapters.title: Salvage Rights
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Bright's crews arrive by barge with generators and cages of recording equipment. Bright offers Felix double forgiveness if she flies reconnaissance for them. She sees the trap clearly for the first time: both sides need her, which means neither can let her leave. Beat: the walls close in.

chapters.title: Sabotage Weather
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She uses her meteorological skill covertly—timing fog banks and gust fronts to stall the Syndicate's equipment—while secretly repairing one radio. Anselm catches her and, instead of exposing her, hands her the expedition's raw data. Beat: alliance across betrayal.

chapters.title: The Storm Remembers
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. The storm reacts to the machinery's noise, swelling off its anchor and beginning to drift downriver—toward the coast, toward towns. Every faction's plan dies at once. Beat: consequence outrunning intention.

chapters.title: What It Found
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In the drifting storm's path she realizes the truth she'd have to tell: the storm isn't responding to humans—it's been listening to the whole watershed, and the drowned valley was its archive. Telling anyone means the archive becomes a target forever. Beat: the full weight of the secret.

chapters.title: One Voice Enough
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Felix flies into the moving storm carrying only a microphone and Anselm's data, planning to speak the valley's own recorded voices back to it—to call it home. Ilsa tries to stop her mid-flight; Bright's crews scramble below. Beat: everything wagered on a single act of witness.

chapters.title: The Long Answer
chapters.summary: Climax. Inside the eye, Felix plays the archive and adds her own voice—her real name, her real debts, her real confession. The storm slows, turns, and settles back onto its anchor as the monsoon breaks around it. Beat: truth offered freely, the thing no faction planned for.

chapters.title: Aftermath Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The Syndicate salvages nothing; Bright's evidence burned in the flood surge, and Felix's testimony sounds like madness. Her debts are voided—not forgiven, just uncollectible against a woman with no proof of anything. Beat: freedom purchased with credibility.

chapters.title: Downriver
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She ferries the surviving expedition members home one by one, lying gently to officials, keeping Ilsa's choice and Anselm's data locked behind her teeth. Ilsa stays upriver, the valley's self-appointed warden. Beat: grief and relief sharing a cockpit.

chapters.title: Emrys
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, epilogue. Months later, grounded and broke but free, she names the storm in her private log after the voice she heard in the eye—Emrys—and files the flight plan for next season. Some things you survive by telling everyone; some by telling no one. Beat: quiet resolve, identity chosen at last.
